IncidentBot: [PING] routing-service: sudden increase in fallback and cross-region assignments detected. metric: cross_region_assign_rate +420% in last 3m. affected path: /v1/chat/completions. severity candidate: SEV2 :rotating_light:
Priya R (oncall): ack. I'm paged in. starting investigation — pinging @Marcos L and @Nico (sre).
Marcos L: on it. quick question: any customer reports?
Jenna (CS): yes, 4 EU accounts opened tickets — increased latency and lower-quality responses. some are getting results from redwood-us-small. sending list in a sec.
Nico (sre): pulling routing-audit logs now. initial grep shows a spike of "tier_mismatch" events being ignored by the assigner for ~2m. threading logs: ```
2023-11-12T09:17:12Z assigner: req=zet01 tenant=ent-99 tenant_tier=enterprise header.tier=enterprise
2023-11-12T09:17:12Z assigner: policy_lookup -> rp-20231110-priority
2023-11-12T09:17:12Z assigner: tiebreak_evaluate -> comparator=hash("user") priority_seq=[cost,latency,tier]
2023-11-12T09:17:12Z assigner: tiebreak_result=cost
2023-11-12T09:17:12Z assigner: assigned_region=us-west assigned_model=redwood-global-small-v2
2023-11-12T09:17:12Z response: 200 (but degraded quality)
```
Priya R (oncall): wait priority_seq shows [cost,latency,tier] — tier is last. That seems wrong for enterprise tenants. Did we flip an ordering?
Marcos L: I see a recent commit in policy engine (PR #7141 merged 2023-11-12T08:50 by infra-bot) that introduced config `default_tiebreak_order`. Looks like a default overwrite applied to all policies without explicit ordering.
InfraBot: deployment: policy-engine v2.9.1 rolled to prod at 2023-11-12T08:55:02Z (commit 9f8b33).
Nico (sre): verifying commits... found change: `if policy.ordering == null then policy.ordering = config.default_tiebreak_order` default set to [cost,latency,tier] in v2.9.1. Previously default was [tier,latency,cost].
Jenna (CS): customers report both latency regressions and content mismatches — enterprise workloads were served by smaller global models in us-west.
Priya R (oncall): immediate mitigation: can we patch policy-engine config to restore tier-first order? or hotfix policy entries for enterprise tenants?
OpsBot: suggested mitigation: run `POST /admin/policies/override` with body `{ "selector": "tenant_tier:enterprise", "ordering": ["tier","latency","cost"] }`. requires admin token.
Marcos L: I can apply tenant-scoped override. running in 30s. will also create a temporary alert to catch any cross_region_assign where tenant_tier=enterprise.
Nico (sre): while Marcos applies the override, I'm watching for ongoing misassigns. also checking whether fallback_model selection logic allows cross-region small variants for enterprise — that's a separate mapping table.
InfraBot: action: applied policy override for selector tenant_tier=enterprise at 2023-11-12T09:20:41Z by Marcos L :white_check_mark:
Marcos L: override applied. telemetry shows immediate drop in cross-region_assigns for enterprise traffic down 95% within 40s.
Priya R (oncall): good. customer impact status? Jenna?
Jenna (CS): enterprise errors dropped from ~12% to ~1.5%. I've messaged the impacted customers that we're mitigating and will provide a postmortem.
Nico (sre): root-cause hypotheses I'm tracking in-thread: H1) default config change in policy-engine v2.9.1 accidentally reordered tiebreakers. H2) fallback model mapping allows cross-region small models for high-tier tenants because mapping rules used `compatibility_level` not `tenant_tier` in lookup. H3) lack of region-scoped canary for policy-engine autopromote (it rolled out global default).
Priya R (oncall): logging evidence for timeline: 
- 08:50 infra-bot PR #7141 merged default_tiebreak_order change
- 08:55 policy-engine v2.9.1 deployed to prod
- 09:12 eu-scheduler reports transient node pressure (spike of pod restarts, 3 nodes degraded)
- 09:17 cross-region_assign spike begins
- 09:20 override applied, mitigation in effect
Nico (sre): adding relevant logs snippet: ```
09:11:45 eu-scheduler: pod eu-infer-07 CrashLoopBackoff -> restarted
09:12:02 routing-service-eu: queue depth +280
09:16:58 policy-eval: rp-20231110-priority -> tie detected among candidates
09:17:12 assigner: comparator used=cost -> selected candidate with smaller model in us-west
09:17:12 trace: fallback_selected=redwood-global-small-v2 assigned_region=us-west
```
Marcos L: immediate post-incident actions: 1) revert default_tiebreak_order to previous value in config store; 2) require explicit ordering in policy manifests; 3) add tenant_tier to model-compat lookup keys.
Priya R (oncall): longer-term mitigations: - region canary for policy-engine autopromote - unit tests for tiebreak ordering semantics - a preflight check that flags policies which could divert enterprise traffic out of region - add SLT (synthetic) checks that validate model mapping quality per tenant tier.
Jenna (CS): I'll prepare customer impact summary and keep watch for any follow-ups.
OpsBot: alert created: cross_region_assign when tenant_tier=enterprise (threshold=1 per min) by Marcos L at 2023-11-12T09:25:05Z :bell:
Nico (sre): opening follow-up tasks: TKT-4010 (policy-engine config audit), TKT-4011 (model-compat mapping fix), TKT-4012 (autopromote canary gating).
Priya R (oncall): severity lowered to SEV3 at 2023-11-12T09:33:00Z — system stabilizing. handing off to day eng.
Marcos L: I'll draft an RCA doc and paste initial timeline + logs into the incident board. tagging this thread for postmortem coordination.
Jenna (CS): updated customers and queued formal communications.
IncidentBot: [CLOSE] incident thread archived for RCA drafting. incident_id=INC-20231112-91.
